fieldMarks: Bulkier than a mourning dove, with a shorter tail; 28-32 cm.
Big white wing patches, most obvious in flight.
White tips on the outer tail feathers.
behavior: Males give crowing calls on spring mornings from streamside groves and desert washes.
Early migrant: most arrive by March and leave in September; a few winter north of Mexico, mainly in towns; Florida birds are mostly resident.
Feeds on wild seeds, grain, acorns and fruit, especially cactus; often perches atop saguaros for fruit and nectar and is an important saguaro pollinator.
May nest in colonies in isolated groves surrounded by good feeding areas.
habitat: Semi-open southwestern habitats: river woods, mesquite, saguaro desert, native Texas brushland, chaparral and open oak woods; adapts readily to farmland, suburbs and citrus groves.
range: Mainly a summer resident in the southwestern United States (California to Texas), with year-round birds in Florida and along the Gulf Coast in winter; expanding northward, with strays far north of the breeding range.

lookalikes.name: Mourning dove
lookalikes.howToTell: The white-winged dove is bulkier and shorter-tailed with large white wing patches.
